scope: Read-only analysis of frozen evidence. Recommendations are hypotheses for later work, not changes to frozen skills or assertions. This pass did not rerun fitting, grade outputs, or independently inspect original image pixels; visual statements are attributed to frozen blind and full-trace reviewers.

comparison_summary.comparator_reasoning: A wins narrowly because its actual mesh has a substantially more upright and source-compatible head/torso than B. Both fail strict pose reconstruction: A still sweeps the upper arms backward with substantial hidden elbow bends, while B adds a pronounced arched/reclined torso and chin tuck, visible even in the photo-camera render and severe in the canonical side. Both retain the original garment construction very well in generated front/closeup, but generated neutral side views normalize the real mesh pose and unobserved backs remain hypotheses. B deserves credit for explicit illustrative pose/depth labels and clearer mesh-parameter provenance, but labels do not offset the worse actual 3D action or pose-role footwear drift. This is a relative winner, not a successful full reconstruction certification.

B better preserves upright asymmetric original stance with a plausible trunk, arm directions and near-straight legs. A is deeply hunched/forward tilted with flexed knees and fingers emerging through pelvis/inner thigh. Both miss the original front-pocket hand placement: B puts that hand against rear hip/buttock. Neither establishes photographed-person dimensions or contact/collision-free status. Full six-image generation is outside this task.

winner_strengths: v1 adds a cross-product reference plus an explicit instruction to rebuild observations and camera/pose priors for each new input. TRACE confirms both v1 executors read it and built new solvers. Both blind reviewers prefer v1 actual torso plausibility; one run per case cannot isolate the reference as the cause.

Pocket v1 uses explicit (bone, axis) mapping and standing root/leg/spine bounds, in contrast to v0 broad spine allowance. Code limits spine01 to ±10°, root ±6°, legs ±12°; full review reports a more upright mesh, whereas v0 final spine01 reaches 68.7°. This is a plausible mechanism for the observed relative posture improvement, not proof of skill causality.

All runs preserve real native Image Gen receipts and original references, use true FK/LBS plus numerical fitting and save consistent complete states. v1 does not gain on those shared integrity criteria.
loser_weaknesses: v0 pocket numerical fit accepts severe torso flexion and hand/pelvis intersection despite a passing visible wrist. v0 boatneck compensates spine02 [-37.8,15.9,17.3] with neck01 [51.3,9.4,5.6], producing reclined chest/chin tuck in frozen visual review.

Neither skill execution converts action-specific hand semantics into a sufficient objective/acceptance check: pocket v1 still puts the hand behind the hip, and both six-view meshes sweep arms backward. This is also a weakness of the relative winner.

Numerical loss, neutral calibration and replay integrity remain insufficient acceptance criteria; every run retains original-region and 3D failures. v1 visible wrists regress despite better shoulder fit.
